title: Stock arrangements of 'Loch Lomond' and the Benny Goodman copy
summary: Jimmy Mundy took the arrangement from her record; the published stock arrangement had Goodman's arrangement credited.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: You told us an anecdote about the stock arrangements of Loch Lomond".

Yes. Well I'm pretty sure by now that everybody knows the story about Benny Goodman and Loch Lomond" -- how when they were out on the road, and they heard the recording that I had made of Loch Lomond" on a juke box somewhere in the middle part of the USA.
Or possibly on the radio show.
Could be, yeah. But anyway, Jimmy Mundy took the arrangement off the -- I'm pretty sure it was off the record.
Because with the record, they'd have an opportunity to play it over and over again. And so

when Benny did this first swing concert at Carnegie Hall, he thought he was introducing Loch Lo-mond." And when Martha Tilton began singing, a lot of the fans in the audience knew that I had been doing it on 52nd Street for -- well, I guess for about six or seven months by that time.
But we were talking about how some of these things happen.

Now Robbins published "Loch Lo-mond." They published a series -- an art series that has my name on it -- "Loch Lomond" As Sung By Maxine Sullivan," and the exact routine that I do with Claude Thornhill's name on it.
But there is a stock arrangement for orchestra that definitely has Benny Goodman's name on it.
Now this sort of shook Al up a little bit.
Yeah. Quite justifiably so, I think.
